strengths: The near-black field, restrained ochre accent, botanical plates and authoritative serif typography create a highly specific coastal horticultural identity rather than a recoloured template.
The plant register is an excellent distinctive device: it turns expertise, site conditions and seasonal performance into visible evidence while giving the site a memorable visual system.
Headlines, project statistics and unusually direct copy communicate conviction and make the studio feel experienced, selective and credible.
Desktop compositions have strong editorial rhythm, disciplined alignment and generous negative space; the pages feel like parts of one coherent publication.
The fixed-price first visit is concrete, well explained and repeatedly presented without undermining the premium tone.

defects.detail: Mobile retains too much desktop density at a very small scale. Navigation, labels, plant metadata, seasonal indicators and footer content become difficult to scan, while the long single-column register creates substantial visual fatigue.

The conversion path is clear at the beginning and end, but long plant and project sequences lack a persistent or well-timed intermediate action. On mobile especially, visitors can travel a great distance after becoming persuaded before encountering the £450 offer again.

On the home page, the extensive register competes with the gardens and paid-visit proposition for overall emphasis; the visual weight implies that plant browsing is the primary task even though booking is the commercial goal.

The no-photography strategy is distinctive and appropriate, but the botanical plates alone provide limited proof that Marram has delivered mature real gardens. Project facts and testimony help, though one or two additional forms of non-photographic evidence would strengthen trust.

The plates are exceptionally well matched to the brand, but their repeated cream rectangles become monotonous in the mobile sequence and occasionally read more like catalogue inventory than art-directed storytelling.
The very small header booking link has limited prominence, particularly on mobile, and does not consistently read as the primary action beside the other navigation items.

summary: This is distinctive, disciplined professional work with unusually strong brand fit and a visual idea that genuinely belongs to Marram. Its principal weakness is mobile pacing: the register becomes a long, densely typeset catalogue, and the paid first visit needs a more accessible re-entry point within that journey.
